2	name: project_slack_telegram_e2e_verify_2026_07_29
3	description: 2026-07-29 — ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (PR #2305, squash 63c7dd519). Chat SDK's pre-dispatch history-cache write silently dropped Telegram/WhatsApp inbound messages; Slack unaffected.

9	---
10	
11	E2E verification of the chat bots on 2026-07-29 (prod `app.lobu.ai`).
12	
13	**Slack: WORKING end-to-end.** Sent a live DM to bot `U095U1QTZ7V` (`@lobu`) in workspace
14	`T09513HDQ77` (lobu-ai.slack.com, connection 390, org `lobu-crm`, agent `crm`).
15	Round trip 30s. Inbound routing, agent dispatch, and outbound reply all fine.
16	The reply was a provider error, not a bot failure:
17	`z.ai returned an error: 429 Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted. Your limit will reset at 2026-07-31 04:32:47`
18	plus a "Manage provider" CTA — i.e. #2280/#2268 error surfacing working as designed
19	(text traces to `packages/server/src/utils/url-builder.ts:260`).
20	A 2026-07-27 DM ("naber") got a real 21s Turkish answer + working
21	"View in Lobu ↗" transcript permalink (#2137), proving the full path when quota is available.
22	
23	**Real blocker = inference quota, not chat.** `lobu-crm` has NO inference-provider
24	connection; the model resolves from server-level Z_AI config. Single provider, no failover
25	→ every agent reply in that org is dead until 2026-07-31 unless a fallback provider is added.
26	See [[project_agent_model_provider_resolution]] and [[project_inference_providers_feature]].
27	
28	**Telegram: was implemented but never connected; now connected in `buremba`.**
29	`packages/connectors/src/telegram.ts` declares `x-lobu-chat-platform: telegram`;
30	`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/platforms/telegram.ts` is a full 401-line impl
31	(webhook secret gen/backfill, cloud-mode polling guard, multi-replica lease), registered in
32	`platforms/index.ts` PLATFORM_REGISTRY. A DB sweep found zero telegram connections anywhere.
33	On 2026-07-29 I created one in org `buremba`: connection **459**, slug
34	`agentconn-85045b7a87884eea`, bot `@burembalobubot` (id 8834276769), agent `personal-agent`,
35	mode `auto` → resolved to webhook `https://app.lobu.ai/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`
36	(confirmed via Telegram `getWebhookInfo`).
37	
38	**TELEGRAM E2E RESULT: INCONCLUSIVE — only ONE real message was ever sent (`/start`), and
39	its pod is gone. Do NOT record this as "Telegram is broken" without a clean retest.**
40	Drove the user's real Chrome (Owletto conn 432) to web.telegram.org and opened
41	`@burembalobubot`. Clicking START sent `/start` at 04:19 (the only genuine send). No reply.
42	**Correction to an earlier conclusion in this session:** three follow-up "messages"
43	(`hello, which agent are you?`, `retest 0330`, `ZZMARKER7391`) were NEVER actually sent —
44	`.message-list-item` contained only `/start`; the text sat in the composer as a draft.
45	`click_ref` on the send button and a synthetic `KeyboardEvent('Enter')` both failed —
46	Telegram's React composer ignores untrusted events. Any "no reply" claim based on those
47	three is void. See [[reference_synthetic_events_dont_send_in_react_composers]].
48	
49	What IS established:
50	- Prod runs revision `049ee2ab` and **#2257 IS deployed** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor
51	  5bc459084 049ee2ab` → true), so the #2230 unrouted-drop fix is live.
52	- #2257 would not cover this case anyway: it patches the **no-agent-resolved** dead end, but
53	  conn 459 has `agent_id: personal-agent`, and `resolveAgentId()`
54	  (`gateway/services/platform-helpers.ts:206`) returns `{source:"connection"}` whenever
55	  `agentId` is set — so the routed path is taken and the unlinked-notice site is never reached.
56	- The route works and IS logged: a manual `curl -X POST` to
57	  `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` appeared in pod logs with `res.status: 401`
58	  (bad secret) — proving requests to that path reach the app and get logged.
59	- Across 2601 log lines on both live pods there is **no** `/lobu/api/v1/webhooks/` entry from
60	  Telegram — but both pods are only ~5 min old and the single real `/start` predates them, so
61	  this proves nothing about that delivery.
62	- The agent is healthy: `conversations.send({agent_id:"personal-agent"})` → `reply: "pong"` in 3.4s.
63	- Prod DOES have a live Z_AI 429: repeated `POST /lobu/api/proxy/z-ai/a/personal-agent/
64	  o/8dc12bdd…/u/watcher_5/chat/completions → 429` in pod logs. So the 429 reaches org
65	  `buremba` too (via watcher_5), even though direct `conversations.send` succeeded.
66	### Deep trace (kubectl, prod) — the `/start` delivery DID arrive and returned 200
67	`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` from **91.108.5.129** (Telegram IP), valid
68	secret header, 288-byte body, **HTTP 200**, on pod `frq5m` at 04:34:11 BST. Also confirmed
69	`[chat-instance-manager] Setting webhook` + `Chat instance started` on `frq5m` ONLY (the
70	other replica `gtzwv` never started it — fine, since hydration is per-request).
71	
72	Every layer verified sound by reading the shipped code — **there is NO Chat SDK gap**:
73	- `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.26.0` `handleWebhook`: verifies secret (timingSafeEqual) → parses
74	  → `processUpdate` → `handleIncomingMessageUpdate` → `chat.processMessage`. Returns 200.
75	- `chat/dist` `dispatchToHandlers`: `isDM` → `directMessageHandlers` → Lobu's handler.
76	- Telegram `isDM(threadId)` = `!chatId.startsWith("-")` → true for a private chat. Correct.
77	- Lobu registers all three handlers (`message-handler-bridge.ts:428-437`): `onNewMention`,
78	  `onDirectMessage`, `onSubscribedMessage`. Correct.
79	- `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` is NOT `silent` in AGENT_ERRORS (`core/src/errors.ts:251`); only
80	  `SESSION_TIMEOUT` is. So a 429 SHOULD post a "Manage provider" card on Telegram too.
81	
82	**Why no reply: `/start` is not a registered Lobu command and is not a normal message.**
83	`getMyCommands` returns new/clear/help/status/try/agents/link — **no `/start`**. Telegram's
84	START button sends exactly `/start`, so it hits the slash-command dispatcher
85	(`message-handler-bridge.ts:1032`), which has no handler for it. Bare `/start` also fails
86	`isBotMentioned` (adapter line ~1206 requires `@username` suffix on a bot_command).
87	`"Processing inbound message"` (the bridge's entry log, :641) never appeared, and 6h of logs
88	across both pods contain **zero** `platform=telegram` turns.
89	NOTE: every early return in `chat/dist handleIncomingMessage` (isMe, dedupe) logs at **debug**,
90	and prod runs at info — so a drop there is invisible. Cannot fully exclude dedupe without
91	raising LOG_LEVEL.
92	
93	### CONFIRMED REPRODUCER (05:10 BST, live pods) — ordinary text message IS silently dropped
94	Sent `KK4477 ping` (plain text, NOT a command) via the browser at 05:10. Verified it really
95	sent: `.message-list-item` shows `KK4477 ping 05:10` and the draft cleared.
96	Pod `summaries-app-lobu-app-b99595f9d-66mxl` logged the delivery:
97	`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`, `cf-connecting-ip: 91.108.5.129` (Telegram),
98	valid `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token`, 279 bytes, **res.status 200**, responseTime 1079ms.
99	**But NO `"Processing inbound message"` and NO `platform=telegram` anywhere after it.**
100	The full 90s log window contains only unrelated `watcher_5`/`platform=api` work.
101	So: adapter accepts + ACKs 200, and the message never reaches
102	`MessageHandlerBridge.handleMessage`. The drop is inside Chat SDK's
103	`handleIncomingMessage` → `dispatchToHandlers`, whose early returns (isMe / dedupe /
104	lock-conflict `handleDrop`) ALL log at **debug** while prod runs at info.
105	`responseTime: 1079ms` is suspiciously long for a 279-byte parse — consistent with the
106	`acquireLock`/state-adapter round-trip in `handleDrop`.
107	PRIME SUSPECT: `handleDrop` lock conflict or the `dedupe:` key in the Postgres state adapter.
108	NEXT DIAGNOSTIC: raise LOG_LEVEL to debug on the app deploy, resend, and read which early
109	return fires. Do NOT guess-fix before that line is seen.
110	
111	**VERDICT: end-to-end is NOT proven, and NOT disproven. `/start` was the wrong test** — it
112	exercises the command path, not the agent path. No ordinary Telegram text message has ever
113	reached this bot (synthetic sends failed, see
114	[[reference_synthetic_events_dont_send_in_react_composers]]).
115	NEXT: a human sends ordinary text (NOT `/start`) to `@burembalobubot`, then
116	`kubectl logs -n summaries-prod summaries-app-lobu-app-<pod> --since=5m | grep -aiE "Processing inbound message|platform=telegram"`.
117	Expect either a turn that 429s (→ Telegram is fine; fix = fallback provider) or a real
118	drop site. Two candidate gaps to fix regardless:
119	1. `/start` should be handled (greet + bind), not silently no-op — Telegram's onboarding
120	   button is the FIRST thing every new user presses.
121	2. `postToPayloadTarget` (`chat-response-bridge.ts:851`) does `if (target) await target.post()`
122	   — a null target silently posts nothing, no log, no throw.
123	
124	### TRAP: `connections.connect()` does NOT start the chat runtime — use `connections.create()`
125	First attempt used `client.connections.connect({connector_key:"telegram", config})`. It returned
126	`status: "active"` with `facets.chat: true` and **no error**, but was completely inert:
127	no webhook registered with Telegram, no `secretToken`, no `chatMetadata`, and
128	`connections.update({agent_id})` failed with *"agent_id applies only to chat connections
129	(it sets the chat runtime's fallback agent); this connection has no chat runtime."*
130	Only `connections.create()` reaches `manage_connections` → `handleCreate`, which checks
131	`options_schema['x-lobu-chat-platform'] === connector_key` and calls
132	`upsertByoChatConnection()` (`gateway/connections/chat-connection-service.ts:235`) —
133	that is what validates the token against the provider, generates `secretToken`, populates
134	`chatMetadata`, and registers the webhook. `connect()` just writes a DB row.
135	An `active` chat connection is therefore NOT proof of a running runtime — verify with the
136	provider (`getWebhookInfo`) or by checking `config.secretToken`/`chatMetadata` exist.
137	Also: `agent_id` is rejected as an argument to create/connect; set it in a follow-up
138	`connections.update({connection_id, agent_id})`.
139	
140	## Gotchas found while verifying
141	- `channel_messages` has NO `direction` column and stores **inbound only** (`is_bot` was
142	  false on every one of 10 rows ever). It cannot prove the bot replied — read the Slack
143	  side (or the conversation transcript) instead.
144	- `channel_messages` only had rows for workspace `T0BCYB6JV3L` (conn 448); the successful
145	  conn-390 DM exchange never appeared there. Absence in that table is NOT evidence of failure.
146	- Two Slack workspaces are live for org `lobu-crm`: conn 390 = `T09513HDQ77` (lobu-ai, the
147	  one the Slack MCP can reach, bot `U095U1QTZ7V`) and conn 448 = `T0BCYB6JV3L` ("LobuSandbox",
148	  enterprise install `E0BDSKL1KJL`, bot `U0BECQZCENR`) — the Slack MCP CANNOT reach 448
149	  (`channel_not_found`).
150	- Slack/Telegram connections live in org `lobu-crm`, NOT `lobu-team` and NOT `buremba`.
151	  Use `query_sql` with `org_slug: "lobu-crm"` to see them.
152	- `client.connections.list()` returns `{connections, total, ...}`, not an array.
153	- `client.conversations.list()` requires `agent_id`; `limit` is rejected.
154	- `information_schema` is not in the queryable allowlist; `SELECT *` on a row to learn columns.
155	- Local dev backend (`:8443`) and the `lobu` CLI (`:8940`) were both down; `.env` here has
156	  no `DATABASE_URL` and `kubectl` has no cluster access. Lobu MCP `query_sql` was the
157	  only working DB path.
158	
159	## RESOLVED — PR #2305 (squash `63c7dd519`), merged 2026-07-29
160	
161	**Root cause.** Chat SDK writes its message-history cache inside `handleIncomingMessage`
162	**before** `dispatchToHandlers`, gated only on the adapter's `persistMessageHistory` flag
163	and with **no try/catch** (`chat/dist/index.js:2966`). `processMessage` catches the throw
164	and the webhook still answers **200**, so a failing *cache* write silently discards the
165	user's message. Only **telegram + whatsapp** set that flag (slack/discord/teams/gchat do
166	not) — exactly why Telegram DMs vanished while Slack worked on the same build. Prod proof:
167	`POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea` from `91.108.5.129`, valid secret, 279 bytes
168	→ **200** in 1079ms, then NO `"Processing inbound message"` and no `platform=telegram`.
169	
170	**Fix.** Normalize the flag off in `ChatInstanceManager.createAdapter()` — the single
171	chokepoint every platform's adapter passes through — via `disableSdkMessageHistory()` in
172	`gateway/connections/platforms/shared.ts`. Removes a write path, does not add one: nothing
173	reads that cache (grep `getMessages`/`msg-history` in packages/server/src → zero consumers).
174	Lobu's durable transcripts are `channel_messages` via `captureChannelMessage` (3 real
175	consumers: manage_feeds, internal conversations route, read_conversation). Also unpinned the
176	hardcoded `logger: "warn"` → honours `LOG_LEVEL`; every SDK silent-drop path logs at `debug`,
177	so the pin made them unreachable at any LOG_LEVEL.
178	Review: bug_free 96, simplicity 95, slop 0, 0 blockers.
179	
180	**Do NOT "add persistMessageHistory everywhere".** It is a capability-compensation flag, not
181	a feature toggle — the SDK's own docstring says to set it only for platforms lacking a
182	server-side history API (WhatsApp, Telegram). Adding it broadly duplicates stale state.
183	
184	**Test:** `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/__tests__/inbound-dispatch-parity.test.ts`
185	drives the REAL Chat SDK through `processMessage`. Red 2 pass/2 fail (both dying at
186	`chat/dist/index.js:2966`); green 3/3. Mutation-tested (`value: false` → `true` re-breaks it).
187	One test deliberately pins the raw-SDK drop so the seam can be deleted if upstream fixes it.
188	
189	**Still open:** ~48 orphaned `msg-history:telegram:6570514069` rows in `chat_state_lists`
190	(prod db `owletto`) are now permanently dead — safe to delete. Separate consolidation worth
191	doing: `ConversationStateStore` vs `channel_messages` are two overlapping history stores
192	(~12 call sites); that is its own branch.
193	
194	## ✅ PROD E2E VERIFIED (2026-07-29 05:50 UTC, deployed `cc269333e` which contains the fix)
195	
196	Sent a correctly-signed Telegram webhook to prod. Full trace on
197	`summaries-app-lobu-app-6cbd9d84bd-*`:
198	```
199	[chat-sdk:telegram]   Telegram adapter initialized { botUserId: '8834276769' }
200	[chat-message-bridge] Processing inbound message          <- NEVER appeared pre-fix
201	[platform-helpers]    Routing to connection's owning agent
202	[user-agents-store]   Added agent personal-agent to user telegram/8450689116
203	[queue-producer]      Enqueued message job 786981, conversation telegram:8450689116
204	[worker] User prompt: POSTFIX9 verify dispatch...
205	```
206	And `channel_messages` now has its FIRST EVER `platform='telegram'` rows — both directions:
207	- id 69 inbound `POSTFIX9 verify dispatch` (is_bot=false)
208	- id 70 **agent reply** (is_bot=true) 7s later
209	
210	Before the fix that same webhook shape returned 200 and produced zero downstream log lines.
211	Slack re-verified unaffected (`Processing inbound message` 2s after a live DM).
212	All four prod pages render (connectors/telegram, activity, memory with Person 4358, agents).
213	
214	Residual (unrelated to this fix): Z_AI quota 429 until 2026-07-31 intermittently fails turns
215	in BOTH orgs. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exists in .env; adding a fallback provider is a prod config
216	change and was left to the user.
217

10	On 2026-05-20 the `summaries-prod` production `owletto` database (49 orgs / 36 users / ~1.17M events, ~12GB) was **wiped**: a developer ran the integration test suite locally with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at prod; `__tests__/setup/test-db.ts` setup runs `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` and the `summaries` role owns the DB, so it succeeded (ran ~16:59–17:27 UTC). NOT CI (CI uses throwaway `lobu_test`).
11	
12	**Recovery:** CNPG PITR from R2 backup lineage `summaries-db-v2` to 2026-05-20 16:00 UTC (latest verified-complete snapshot) into a NEW cluster **`lobu-ai-prod-db`** (clean name chosen by user). The old `summaries-db` was retired/deleted.
13	
14	**Current prod topology (CNPG on k8s, ns `summaries-prod`):**
15	- DB cluster `lobu-ai-prod-db` + pooler `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` + daily ScheduledBackup; backups to R2 serverName `lobu-ai-prod-db`.
16	- GitOps-managed at `packages/owletto/deploy/k8s/apps/lobu-db/` via its OWN Flux Kustomization `lobu-db` (separate path so it escapes the lobu app overlay's `summaries-` namePrefix → keeps the clean name). The lobu app overlay (`apps/lobu/overlays/summaries-prod`) no longer defines a DB; app+migrate `poolerService` point at `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` / `lobu-ai-prod-db-rw`.
17	- App DB creds secret `summaries-db-app` (NOT cluster-owned — survives cluster deletion). R2 creds `summaries-r2-backup-credentials` (SealedSecret).
18	
19	**Prevention shipped (lobu#989, merged `df38fbf4`):** `getTestDb()` refuses any DB whose name isn't test-shaped (`assertSafeTestDatabaseUrl`; override `LOBU_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TEST_DB=1`); baseline `00000000000000_baseline.sql` `migrate:down` is now `RAISE EXCEPTION` (was `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`). owletto #208 (cutover) + #209 (GitOps codify) merged.
20	
21	**PITR recovery runbook lessons (do these BEFORE cutover next time):** (1) PITR resets planner statistics → run `ANALYZE` or queries seq-scan and time out (`resolve_path` hit this). (2) A hand-made recovery cluster has NONE of the chart's tuning/resources — copy `shared_buffers`/`random_page_cost=1.1`/`effective_cache_size`/resources from the chart. (3) `geo_earthdistance` migration needs `cube`+`earthdistance` extensions pre-created as superuser (app role can't CREATE untrusted earthdistance) and conflicts with pre-squash `geo_lookup(p_lat,…)` (`DROP FUNCTION` it first). (4) CNPG `bootstrap` is immutable — a GitOps manifest adopting an existing recovered cluster MUST replicate its exact bootstrap or the webhook rejects the apply. (5) Flux `prune: true` on the apps Kustomization — removing a cluster from render deletes it; verify `kustomize build` before merge.

content.text:
Checked prod end to end. Short version: the pipeline is working right now, and your bot has just replied to your real Telegram chat twice — go look at @burembalobubot, you should see two messages that arrived at 12:36 and 12:37 UTC.

What I found:

**The #2305 fix is genuinely deployed.** Prod runs `e89f82c18` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 63c7dd519 e89f82c18` → true; `disableSdkMessageHistory` is present in the deployed tree.

**Your 12:31 message did reach the server but never became a message.** One and only one Telegram delivery in the last 4h:
```
12:31:25 [connection-routes] Inbound platform webhook
[chat-sdk:telegram] Telegram adapter initialized { botUserId: '8834276769' }
12:31:26 Setting webhook / Interaction bridge registered / Chat instance started
POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea  from 91.108.5.129, 271 bytes, 200, 1134ms
```
and then nothing — no `Processing inbound message`, and critically **no `dedupe:telegram:6570514069:<id>` row was written** in `chat_state_cache`. That matters: dedupe is written *inside* the SDK's inbound path, so this update never entered it at all. That's a different failure point from the #2305 bug (which dropped *after* dedupe).

**I then replayed a correctly-signed webhook against your real chat id (6570514069), not the synthetic one used this morning:**
- plain text `DIAG1 synthetic realchat` → `Processing inbound message` → `Routing to connection's owning agent` → `Enqueued message job 793043, conversation telegram:6570514069` → agent replied 4s later. `channel_messages` id 71 (inbound) + 72 (bot reply).
- `/start` → `Processing inbound message` → `Dispatching command` → replied. So `/start` is handled now too.

Both wrote dedupe rows; both logged `Response completed via Chat SDK bridge`. So inbound routing, agent dispatch, and outbound delivery to *your* chat all work on the current build.

So the remaining question is what that 271-byte payload actually was. It's too short to be `/start` (287 bytes with the `bot_command` entity, and `/start` would have logged a dispatch anyway) and consistent with a ~4–5 char text message — but a plain text message from that chat demonstrably works. The other reading is that it wasn't a `message` update at all (e.g. `my_chat_member` from re-opening the bot, or an edited/reaction update), which the adapter ignores silently. I can't tell from the outside because prod logs at info and every SDK skip path logs at debug.

Confidence: 85 on "the fix is deployed and the full Telegram path works for your chat" — basis: live prod trace with your real chat id, both DB directions, and a delivered reply, not a typecheck. 35 on "we know why the 12:31 delivery vanished" — I have the request line and the absence of a dedupe write, but not the payload.

Next actions, pick one:
1. Send one ordinary text to @burembalobubot now and tell me — I'll tail both pods live and catch the raw request; if it's the same silent drop I'll have a real reproducer this time.
2. Tell me whether you see the two bot replies in Telegram (that confirms outbound is fine and narrows this to inbound-only).
3. Set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the app deploy for a few minutes so the SDK's skip paths become visible — it's a prod env change (Flux-managed, so it'll revert), your call.
4. Separately worth doing regardless: the webhook route logs `Inbound platform webhook` but nothing about *what kind* of update was dropped — an info-level "update ignored, type=X" would have answered this in one line.

11	Driving a React chat composer (Telegram Web `web.telegram.org/a/`) via the Owletto Chrome
12	bridge: text can be typed into the composer successfully, but **submitting it silently fails**.
13	
14	Both of these produced NO sent message on Telegram Web (2026-07-29):
15	- `click_ref` on the send button from a fresh `get_accessibility_tree` snapshot
16	- `evaluate` dispatching `new KeyboardEvent('keydown'|'keypress'|'keyup', {key:'Enter',
17	  keyCode:13, bubbles:true, cancelable:true})` on the contenteditable
18	
19	React ignores events with `isTrusted: false` for send, so the text just stays in the composer
20	as a draft. **The failure is invisible** — `document.body.innerText` still shows your text
21	(because the draft renders inline near the message list), so a naive "did my text appear on
22	the page?" check reports success and you conclude the remote side dropped the message.
23	
24	**Verify a send by the message list, never by page text:**
25	`[...document.querySelectorAll('.message-list-item')].map(m => m.innerText)` — the text must
26	appear THERE. Also check for a `MessageOutgoingStatus` node. A populated
27	`#editable-message-text` after a "send" means it never sent.
28	
29	This cost a wrong conclusion in this session: three "unanswered" Telegram messages had never
30	actually been sent, which nearly got recorded as a server-side silent-drop bug.
31	See [[project_slack_telegram_e2e_verify_2026_07_29]].
32	
33	**IT DOES WORK — the real trap is `filter: "interactive"` on the a11y tree.**
34	Later in the same session I sent Telegram messages successfully via the Owletto bridge. The
35	send button is **absent from `get_accessibility_tree` with `filter: "interactive"`**, while a
36	*different* button ("Go to bottom") sits at almost the same coordinates — so geometry-based or
37	fuzzy-name matching clicks the wrong element and silently does nothing.
38	
39	Recipe that works:
40	1. `get_accessibility_tree` with **`filter: "all"`** (not "interactive").
41	2. Find the composer by exact name match: `(n.name||'').trim().toLowerCase() === 'message'`.
42	3. `click_ref` it, then `type_ref` the text.
43	4. Re-snapshot with `filter: "all"` (the send button only appears once there is text).
44	5. Find send by **exact** name: `=== 'send message'`. Never fuzzy-match `/send/i` and never
45	   fall back to bounding-box proximity — both hit "Go to bottom".
46	6. `click_ref` it, then confirm via `.message-list-item` + an emptied composer.
47	
48	Note `Object.defineProperty`-style state: after each send the epoch changes, so always
49	re-snapshot before the next interaction rather than reusing a stale `document_epoch`.
50	
51	Direct API is still no substitute for an inbound test: for a bot you own, `sendMessage` posts
52	AS the bot, so it cannot simulate the human side.

# Browser-driven verification (authenticated)

For any UI verification that needs a signed-in session (past the auth wall), use the `agent-browser` CLI with a session cookie minted from the DB. The user's regular Chrome doesn't expose a remote-debug port, so `--auto-connect` will land on the wrong tab — mint a cookie instead.

## Scope

The forged session cookie authenticates the **web admin REST mounted at `/`** (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/<orgSlug>/...`, the SPA — anything `lobu apply` and the web app talk to). It does **NOT** authenticate the **public Agent API at `/lobu`** (`/lobu/api/v1/agents/*`, `/lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/sessions`) — that path expects a JWT bearer from the OAuth device flow (`lobu login`) or a PAT. If `/lobu/api/v1/agents` returns `401` despite a valid cookie, switch to `lobu chat` / `lobu token`.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)

# Session token from the DB (prod DB serves both targets)
DB="$(grep '^DATABASE_URL=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)"
TOKEN=$(psql "$DB" -tAc "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash
SIGNED=$(SECRET="$SECRET" TOKEN="$TOKEN" node -e '
  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Drive the browser

```bash
agent-browser --session lobu-verify open "https://app.lobu.ai/"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify eval "document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=$SIGNED; path=/; secure; samesite=lax'"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify open "https://app.lobu.ai/<path>"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify wait --text "<expected text>" --timeout 25000
agent-browser --session lobu-verify snapshot -i      # find @refs
agent-browser --session lobu-verify click @e13        # interact
agent-browser --session lobu-verify screenshot --full /tmp/out.png
agent-browser --session lobu-verify close
```

## Driving the paired Owletto extension (connector debugging)

The cookie-forging above and `claude-in-chrome` both drive a *separate* browser that lacks the user's real logged-in sessions — Revolut, for instance, redirects them to `sso.revolut.com/signin`. To run JS or browser actions in the **paired Owletto extension** (the Chrome that holds the user's live sessions, which is what extension-scrape connectors like Revolut/LinkedIn use), go through the connector-operations bridge instead. No deploy required.

`lobu connector run` is the wrong tool here — it only does local Playwright/CDP against a `browser_session` auth profile, so it errors `Missing --auth-profile` for device-worker connectors (Revolut has no auth profile).

For one-off actions, the `lobu call` CLI is the quickest path (usually org `buremba`; connection id from `lobu call manage_connections --org buremba --arg action=list --raw`):

```bash
lobu call manage_operations --org buremba --arg action=execute \
  --arg connection_id=<chrome-connection-id> --arg operation_key=navigate \
  --arg input:='{"url":"https://app.slack.com/...","wait_for_load":true,"open_in_new_tab":true}' --raw
```

For multi-step scripts, use the SDK `operations` namespace via `lobu memory exec` / `run_sdk`:

```js
// chrome connection id: client.connections.list() → connector_key 'chrome'
const ops = await client.operations.listAvailable({ connection_id: CHROME_CONN_ID });
// navigate opens a fresh background tab in the paired Chrome and returns tab_id
const nav = await client.operations.execute({
  connection_id: CHROME_CONN_ID, operation_key: 'navigate',
  input: { url: 'https://app.revolut.com/transactions', open_in_new_tab: true, wait_for_load: true },
});
// evaluate runs arbitrary JS on that tab and returns the JSON-serialised result
await client.operations.execute({
  connection_id: CHROME_CONN_ID, operation_key: 'evaluate',
  input: { tab_id: nav.output.tab_id, expression: '(async()=>{ /* read DOM */ return out })()', await_promise: true },
});
```

`operations.execute` → `dispatchChromeActionToExtension` (`worker-api/dispatch-chrome-action.ts`) → device-worker queue → the paired extension — the same bridge the office-bot Deliveroo connector uses. Chrome ops: `navigate`, `evaluate`, `get_accessibility_tree`, `wait_for_selector`, `click_ref`, `type_ref`, `screenshot`, `show_notification`, `network_intercept_*`, `close_tab`.

Gotchas:
- `search_sdk operations` surfaces the `operations` namespace and current method signatures. Use `Object.keys(client)` inside a `run_sdk` script only when checking discovery/runtime parity.
- Sessions that re-auth often (Revolut, ~hourly) must be freshly logged in *in the paired Chrome* right before you navigate+evaluate, or the fresh tab redirects to the sign-in wall.
- Per-call dispatch latency is 5–60s and virtualized lists recycle content out — for paginated scrapes, iterate inside the connector's own run, not via one-shot `evaluate`s.
- **Connector-side changes ship via re-apply, not the app release.** Per-org connectors (`examples/personal-agent`) live in `connector_definitions`/`connector_versions` and only update on `lobu apply` (or `connections.installConnector` for a single bundle). An app deploy that adds a *capability* (e.g. `show_notification`) does nothing until the connector that *calls* it is re-applied. **And a new chrome action also needs the matching handler in the extension build** — dispatching `show_notification` to an older installed extension fails with `Owletto for Chrome: unknown dispatch ... action_key='show_notification'`. So three things gate such a notification: an up-to-date extension build (the handler), a re-applied connector (the call), and macOS notification permission on the extension.

{operation_key:'focus_tab', input:{tab_id}}` before the identical snapshot→click sequence sent
it immediately. So a "clicked" result from the bridge is NOT evidence of a send — only
`.message-list-item` is. Sequence that works: navigate → focus_tab → tree(all) → click_ref
composer → type_ref → tree(all) → click_ref 'send message' → verify `.message-list-item`.

The `ref` argument is an OBJECT: `{ref_id, document_epoch}` — both come from the
`get_accessibility_tree` output (`output.tree[]` rows carry `ref_id`; `output.document_epoch`
is top-level). Passing the DOM id string errors `ref: must be object`. Also: the send button
only enters the tree once the composer actually holds text, and the type can lag the snapshot —
if 'send message' is missing, sleep and re-snapshot rather than concluding it isn't there.

content.text:
Dug into all three. Answers in order.

## What `chat_state_cache` is

It's the Chat SDK's key-value store, and we own the implementation. The SDK (`chat` 4.26.0, a 123KB npm dep) defines a `StateAdapter` interface; `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/state-adapter.ts` (400 lines) implements it against our postgres-js pool, backing five tables — `chat_state_cache`, `_lists`, `_queues`, `_subscriptions`, `_locks` — plus `chat_user_identities`. The header comment explains why we didn't use `@chat-adapter/state-pg`: it needs a `pg.Pool`, we speak postgres-js everywhere, and carrying node-postgres plus a second pool to satisfy one library was worse than 400 lines of CRUD. Schemas match state-pg's so it's swappable. That call looks right to me.

What's actually in it in prod today, all under `key_prefix = 'chat-conn'`:

```
cache   conversation_index  7155     ← Lobu's, not the SDK's
cache   session             7155     ← Lobu's
cache   dedupe               297     ← SDK: inbound message-id, 5min TTL
cache   thread-backfilled     31
cache   slack                 12
cache   history_index          8
lists   slack                239
lists   history              143     ← Lobu's sliding window
lists   msg-history           48     ← SDK's, DEAD since #2305
locks                          0
subs                          68
```

Two different things share one store. `dedupe:`/`msg-history:`/`thread-backfilled:` are the SDK's internals. `session:`, `conversation_index:`, `history:`, `history_index:` are **ours** — `ConversationStateStore` (352 lines) writes Lobu's own ThreadSession mapping and a 10-message/24h-TTL context window through the SDK's KV interface. 7155 rows each of `session:` and `conversation_index:`, TTL'd, in a KV table, is Lobu domain data living in a borrowed cache. That's the part I'd question, not the adapter.

The `dedupe:` key is also the most useful debugging tripwire in the system — it's written inside the SDK's inbound path, so its presence or absence tells you which side of the SDK boundary a message died on. That's how I established this morning's "hey" died *before* the SDK's inbound path, i.e. somewhere different from the #2305 bug.

## Yes, we do workarounds — four real ones

**1. `disableSdkMessageHistory` (`platforms/shared.ts:26`)** — `Object.defineProperty` over a flag the SDK declares readonly, because the SDK writes its history cache before dispatch, unguarded, and `processMessage` swallows the throw while still answering 200. That's #2305. It's a patch on a third-party bug, applied at our one chokepoint.

**2. Synthesizing the SDK's private `_currentMessage`** (`chat-response-bridge.ts:61-70, 886`). Comment: *"Passing `{}` crashes the SDK; passing `undefined` silently disables the recipient hint."* We hand-build a Message-shaped object to keep `handleStream` from throwing on `.author.userId`, which it reads unconditionally.

**3. Calling `createThread`, which isn't on the public type** — `const createThread = (chat as any).createThread` then `.call(chat, adapter, threadId, currentMessage, false)`, four positional args including a bare boolean (`platforms/shared.ts:63`). We're bound to that call signature with no type protection.

**4. `resolveChatTarget`** — a four-step fallback dance (responseThreadId → DM shortcut → thread → last-resort channel) because there's no straight "reply to this message" primitive. The last step exists specifically "so the response still lands somewhere instead of silently disappearing."

To be fair, the codebase is disciplined about it — only 8 `as any` in the whole connections tree. These aren't sloppiness, they're a thin SDK meeting a product that needs more than it offers. But 1 and 2 are patches on SDK defects, and 3 is a private-API dependency that a minor version bump can break silently.

## The queue is not the overengineered part

`runs-queue.ts` is 933 lines and it's one Postgres table with `SKIP LOCKED` claims, `pg_notify` wakeups on a shared LISTEN socket, a heartbeat, and a stale-claim sweeper. Producer is 99 lines. For durable, multi-replica, at-least-once delivery that's close to the minimum honest implementation — no broker, no second datastore, and the per-queue NOTIFY channels avoid a thundering herd. I'd leave it alone.

What's heavy is everything around it. One "hey" traverses: webhook route → `ensureConnectionRunning` (DB read + possible instance hydration) → SDK verify/parse/dedupe/dispatch → `MessageHandlerBridge` (1613 lines: resolve agent, apply settings, capture transcript) → INSERT into `runs` + notify → claim loop on some pod → `message-consumer` (1271) → `deployment-manager` (2699, spawns a child process) → worker connects back over SSE → `chat-response-bridge` (904) → `resolveChatTarget` → post. That's 13,029 lines in `gateway/connections` plus 5,145 in `orchestration` wrapping a 123KB SDK. It does run in 4-5 seconds, so it's not slow — but it's a lot of surface for a message to cross, and this morning's drop happened in a seam nobody logs at info level.

The concrete redundancy I'd point at: **three history stores for the same conversation.** `channel_messages` (durable, what feeds/search/`read_conversation` actually read), `chat_state_lists` `history:` (our 10-message window, 143 rows), and the SDK's `msg-history:` (48 orphan rows, dead since #2305). Two are load-bearing for different readers and one is garbage. That's the consolidation branch already noted as owed.

Confidence: **85** on the `chat_state_cache` description and the workaround inventory — I read the implementations and counted the prod rows. **60** on the queue verdict — I read `runs-queue.ts`'s design and the producer end to end, but I traced `deployment-manager` only at the header level, so "the orchestration is where the weight is" is a size-and-shape judgment, not a line-by-line audit.

Next actions:
1. Delete the 48 dead `msg-history:telegram:6570514069` rows — they're unreachable since #2305 and they confused this morning's diagnosis.
2. Add the info-level "update ignored, type=X" log in `handleWebhook`. Cheapest possible fix for the class of bug that has now bitten twice, and it would have answered the "hey" question in one line.
3. Pin the `createThread` reach-in behind a typed wrapper with a startup assertion, so a `chat` minor bump fails loudly at boot instead of silently at reply time.
4. The `ConversationStateStore` vs `channel_messages` consolidation (~12 call sites) — its own branch, and worth scoping before it grows a third reader.

Spent the time to actually measure this rather than guess. Short answer: **removing the Chat SDK would increase complexity, not reduce it.** But there are three consolidations worth real money, and one of them is the thing that bit you this morning.

## Why dropping it loses

The SDK's footprint is much smaller than the 13k lines around it suggests. Exactly **10 files** import from `chat`, and the surface is four things: the `Chat` class (2 files), the card DSL `Card/CardText/Actions/Button/LinkButton` (4 files), the `StateAdapter` type (we implement it), and `CardElement`.

So I checked what would actually get deleted. `chat-instance-manager.ts` is 2,604 lines and only about six of its ~50 methods touch the SDK — `startInstanceUnscoped`, `handleWebhook`, `postMessageToChannel`, `createStateAdapter`, the react/edit/delete trio. Everything else is connection CRUD, row-versioned hydration, multi-replica claim/lease, the exclusive runner, health sweeps, secret normalization. **All of that survives SDK removal unchanged.** Same for `message-handler-bridge` (agent routing), the queue, the orchestrator. You'd delete the adapters and inherit their job.

And that job is bigger than it looks, because of the card DSL. `Card`/`Button`/`LinkButton` have **67 call sites**, and they're not confined to chat — they're in notifications, guardrails, approval prompts, the activity feed, `manage_behaviors`. That DSL is the vocabulary the whole product uses to render an interactive message, and the SDK compiles it to Block Kit for Slack and inline keyboards for Telegram. Replacing it means writing a per-platform renderer and touching 67 sites. That's the SDK's real value and it's the expensive part to reproduce.

The breadth argument also runs the other way from what you'd expect. Per-platform modules cost: whatsapp 16 lines, gchat 17, teams 22, discord 22, slack 100, telegram 401. Six platforms for ~600 lines of ours. Breadth is nearly free *because* of the SDK — dropping it is what would make each additional platform expensive.

Worth knowing: prod runs two platforms. Slack (3 active, 5 paused) and Telegram (1). `channel_messages` has 68 slack rows and 12 telegram. Discord/Teams/GChat/WhatsApp have never had a connection. I'm **not** suggesting you delete them — low usage isn't delete evidence, and they're advertised product surface. I mention it because it means the SDK's six-platform breadth is currently carrying two, so "the abstraction earns its keep across many platforms" isn't the argument for keeping it. The card DSL is.

## What's actually worth consolidating

**1. Get Lobu's data out of the SDK's KV.** This is the big one. `chat_state_cache` holds 7,155 `session:` rows and 7,155 `conversation_index:` rows — those are Lobu's ThreadSession mapping, not the SDK's. Plus 143 `history:` list rows. We're storing first-class domain data in a TTL'd key-value store we borrowed from a third-party library, through that library's interface. It deserves a real table with a real schema and no expiry. This also decouples our data from SDK lifecycle entirely, so the next `chat` bump can't reach it.

**2. Collapse three history stores into one.** Right now the same conversation is recorded in `channel_messages` (durable, what feeds/search/`read_conversation` actually read), `chat_state_lists` `history:` (a 10-message/24h window for agent context), and the SDK's `msg-history:` (48 rows, dead since #2305). Two serve different readers, one is garbage. Making `ConversationStateStore.getHistory` a query over `channel_messages` removes a store and a sync problem. ~12 call sites.

**3. Put every SDK reach-in behind one seam with a boot assertion.** We have four of them — the `Object.defineProperty` over the readonly `persistMessageHistory`, the synthesized private `_currentMessage`, the untyped `(chat as any).createThread` called with four positional args, and the `resolveChatTarget` fallback dance. They're spread across `platforms/shared.ts` and `chat-response-bridge.ts`. One module owning all four, with a startup check that those private members still exist, converts "SDK minor bump silently drops replies" into "pod fails to boot." Given #2305 cost a full session and this morning cost another, that's cheap insurance.

One more thing that argues against the SDK-as-single-door model: we already bypass it where it doesn't fit. `slack-web.ts` is a 283-line dependency-free fetch wrapper whose header says explicitly *"NOT `@slack/web-api`, NOT the chat adapter"* — used for onboarding DMs and the authz channel-membership sync. That's the right instinct, and it's evidence the boundary should be "SDK owns wire protocol and card rendering, we call the platform directly for everything else," stated deliberately rather than discovered case by case.

Confidence: **80**. Basis: I counted the import surface, the card call sites, the per-platform line costs, the method inventory of `chat-instance-manager`, and the live prod connection/message counts per platform. What I did *not* do is prototype removing an adapter, so "reproducing Block Kit rendering is the expensive part" is a reasoned estimate from 67 call sites, not a measured one.

Next actions:
1. Scope the `session:`/`conversation_index:` migration out of `chat_state_cache` into a real table — 14,310 rows, and it's the change that most reduces coupling.
2. Fold `ConversationStateStore.getHistory` into a `channel_messages` query and delete the 48 dead `msg-history:` rows in the same branch.
3. The SDK-seam module plus boot assertion — smallest of the three, highest ratio of risk removed to lines written.
4. If you want a real answer on the SDK long-term, the honest test is whether the card DSL ever needs to express something Slack and Telegram can't both render. That's when the abstraction starts costing more than it saves, and it's worth watching for rather than deciding now.

47	
48	## ⭐ MODEL CLARIFIED 2026-06-26 — connection = queryable source; Feed = view generated on the fly; 3 KINDS
49	User's settled framing (the real "3 types of feed"): **a Connection is a queryable source (Postgres-like).** A **Feed is a VIEW over it, generated on the fly** at access time — NOT a stored row by default. Materialization is an optimization, not the model. Three feed KINDS, by WHERE the data lives:
50	1. **chat channel** → `channel_messages` (live conversation transcript).
51	2. **virtual live dataset** → an EXTERNAL source queried LIVE; generated on the fly, NOT copied into `events`. ⚠️ CORRECTION 2026-06-26 (then refined): I wrongly called this "design"; user caught it. Then over-corrected to "exists" — the PRECISE status (per `docs/database-connectors.md`): the connector `query()` LIVE-READ (no copy) + `QueryContext` "virtual-feed read" (`connector-types.ts:842`) + connection-backed live derived entities **SHIP (#1182)**, metrics run live against them. BUT the user-facing **`virtual` FEED FLAG** (+ `search()` + fan-out) is **"Slice 2 / next" = remaining work**. So virtual-live-dataset = **PARTIAL** (live-read infra yes; feed-flag surface no). **Authoritative docs: `docs/database-connectors.md` (postgres connector + virtual feeds + tiers/egress), `docs/define-metric-design.md` (metric lens).** My `docs/plans/feeds-and-connections-model.md` is the cross-cutting model and now cross-references both. Unbuilt: the `virtual` feed flag AND the unified `FeedReader<S,L>` registry.
52	3. **collected** → `events` (sync materializes rows; the classic data feed = real row in `feeds`).
53	**Orthogonal axis = READ LENS (how you query a feed), independent of kind:** `recall` (fuzzy retrieval, `search_memory`, BUILT this PR) · `metric` (aggregation → `metric_series`, existing) · `query_sql` (raw scoped SQL via `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA`→`buildScopedQuery` CTEs, existing). So: kind = where data lives; lens = query shape; any lens over any kind.
54	**Why this matters for the shipped recall registry:** the `RecallSource[]` registry IS the read side. Today 2 sources (knowledge=events, conversation=channel_messages). When the **virtual-live-dataset** kind lands, recall gains a 3rd source = ONE array entry, no `if/else` — that generic-abstraction payoff is exactly why the user pushed for it. Architecture artifact: /tmp/conversation-feeds-architecture.html (ephemeral). NONE of the 3-kind Feed abstraction is built; only the recall read-side over the 2 existing stores is.
55	**FINALIZED 2026-06-26 (codex high-reasoning consulted, agreed):** keep KIND and LENS **orthogonal** — do NOT collapse into one enum (combinatorial explosion / capability gaps). Unifying abstraction = a generated query/view parameterized by (source, shape, lens), realized as a **capability registry keyed by the `(sourceKind, lensKind)` tuple** — `FeedReader<S,L>` with `canRead`/`read`, dispatch by tuple, missing combos = explicit unsupported capabilities not enum holes; materialization = source-adapter implementation detail. Shipped `RecallSource[]` = the `lens=recall` row; generalize `RecallSource → FeedReader` only when a 3rd kind/2nd lens needs the registry (not now). Written up: `docs/plans/feeds-and-connections-model.md` (DESIGN doc, in this branch).
56	
57	## The core architectural decision: Feed is an INTERFACE, not a table
58	Two implementations behind one interface; **keep the physical tables separate — do NOT add a `kind` column to the `feeds` table and stuff conversations in** (that makes `feeds` a sparse god-table: checkpoint/schedule/repair_agent_id all NULL for conversations).
59	
60	```
61	Feed {
62	  id; kind: 'data' | 'conversation';
63	  label; status; lastActivityAt;
64	  recentActivity(since) -> items;   // THE shared seam (see below)
65	  target?;                          // routed agent (conversation feeds only)
66	}
67	```
68	- **data feed** — backed by the `feeds` table; items in `events`. (Exists today.)
69	- **conversation feed** — **VIRTUAL**, projected at query time from `channel_messages` (group by `connection_id, channel_id`); `target` decorated from `agent_channel_bindings`. **No row in the `feeds` table.**
70	
71	**`recentActivity(since)` is what earns the abstraction (not card rendering).** One method, two consumers:
72	1. the connection rail's "last active" line (THIS project), and
73	2. the runtime "what happened in between" context block (follow-up, see Stage B).
74	Data feeds implement it over `events`; conversation feeds over `channel_messages`. If the only shared thing were "renders as a card", it'd be a view-model, not a domain abstraction — `recentActivity` makes it real.
75	**YAGNI discipline:** only ONE new kind (conversation) exists. Build the interface + the conversation impl; let existing data feeds be the 2nd impl that proves the seam. Do NOT build a generalized "virtual feed plugin registry" until a 3rd kind (email threads, etc.) appears. Design the seam, not the framework.
76	
77	## Storage split (settled, but confirm exact semantics with user — see OPEN #1)
78	- **Conversation (raw messages, DMs, backfill + live) -> `channel_messages`.** Keep this table AS-IS. It is purpose-built: connection-scoped transcript, compliance-DELETABLE, cheap recency queries. NOT `events`.
79	- **Promoted / distilled knowledge / non-message signal -> `events`.** Via the EXISTING seam (agent `save_memory` / watcher distillation). The `channel_messages` migration comment LITERALLY states this design: *"messages worth remembering are PROMOTED into events separately… keeping the knowledge store curated."*
80	- **Do NOT bulk-embed every Slack message into `events`** — that re-triggers the documented embed-backfill congestion incidents (single-threaded embeddings pod, 30s timeouts). Backfill goes to `channel_messages` (no embeddings); promotion to `events` stays selective/bounded.
81	
82	## Slack granularity mapping
83	| Slack | Model |
84	|---|---|
85	| Workspace (team) + bot install | **Connection** (`agent_connections`, `platform='slack'`, team in metadata) |
86	| Channel / DM / group-DM (`im`/`mpim`) | **Feed** (durable container = routing unit = `channel_messages` group key) |
87	| Thread (`thread_id`) | conversation/run within the feed (the item) |
88	| Message | `channel_messages` row |
89	Why channel-not-thread: feed must be stable/manageable/routable; binding routes on `channel_id` not `thread_id`; thread-as-feed explodes the list into thousands. (Could allow opt-in "pin a thread as a feed" later.)
90	
91	## GROUND TRUTH verified this session (don't re-investigate)
92	- `channel_messages` schema — `db/migrations/20260618130000_channel_messages.sql:17`: cols `id, organization_id, connection_id text, platform, channel_id, thread_id, platform_message_id, author_id, author_name, is_bot, text, occurred_at, created_at`; UNIQUE(connection_id, channel_id, platform_message_id). Hot index `20260618130010`: `(organization_id, connection_id, channel_id, occurred_at DESC)` — exactly the shape for feed-list + `recentActivity(since)`. **Has `connection_id` -> conversation feeds project per-connection with NO join.**
93	- Written by `captureChannelMessage` — `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/channel-transcript.ts:71` (gated by `recordChannelMessages` setting). Read backend for the `read_conversation`/`get_channel_history` tool.
94	- Routing: `resolveAgentId` — `packages/server/src/gateway/services/platform-helpers.ts:247` (binding -> connection.agent -> drop; `crossOrg` flag uses `getBindingAnyOrg` for preview). Bindings table `agent_channel_bindings` (`db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:347`) keyed `(organization_id, platform, channel_id, team_id) -> agent_id`; **has NO `connection_id`** (so "bound-but-silent" channels need an `(org,platform,team_id)` derivation; channels WITH messages don't, via channel_messages.connection_id).
95	- Binding service / channels API: `packages/server/src/gateway/channels/binding-service.ts`; `packages/server/src/gateway/routes/public/channels.ts` (GET/POST/DELETE `/api/v1/agents/{agentId}/channels`). UI today: `packages/owletto/src/components/agents/agent-channels-index.tsx` (preview-link cards only, raw `channel_id` shown, no per-connection surface).
96	- Feeds (data) model: table `feeds` (`baseline.sql:1450`), `FeedDefinition` (`packages/connector-sdk/src/connector-types.ts:411`), frontend `FeedItem` (`packages/owletto/src/lib/api/connections.ts:151`), device-feed routes `/api/workers/me/feeds` (`packages/server/src/index.ts:928`, handlers `worker-api/device-feeds.ts`). Feeds already do **per-instance via config** (device feeds key on `config.folder_id`) — same pattern a per-channel instance would use.
97	- Feeds UI to reuse (presentation only): rail `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-feeds-rail.tsx`; add-form `.../add-feed-form.tsx`.
98	- Slack connector is `kind:'integration'`, **no feeds, no sync()** — `packages/connectors/src/slack.ts:73` (header says "Slack is a CHAT platform, not a data feed"). Has read scopes `channels:history,groups:history,im:history,mpim:history,users:read` + `message.*` event subs, used ONLY for live chat. **No `conversations.list/history` ingestion exists today.** `getLiveConversationHistory` (chat-instance-manager) reads one convo on-demand.
99	- Delivery dispatch already generic: `deliveryKind: 'data' | 'chat'` (`connector-types.ts:180`) — engine dispatches on this, never a provider name.
100	- Runtime system context is **STATIC ONLY** — `packages/agent-worker/src/openclaw/session-context.ts:196` (`getOpenClawSessionContext`): identity/soul, platform+network+skills instructions, MCP tools/status/context, providerConfig. Cached 5min (`:220`). **NOTHING situational** (no recent activity / no "since last run" delta). This is the gap for the in-between-context goal.
101	- "Chat SDK" = third-party `@chat-adapter/*` v4.26.0 + `chat` pkg (`packages/server/package.json`), NOT Vercel. Web chat render = `@assistant-ui/react` + native SSE (`owletto/.../lobu-runtime-provider.tsx:489`). **Vercel AI SDK is NOT used anywhere.**
102	- Rendering paths: (A) `json_template` rich DSL (44 node types, `owletto/src/lib/json-renderer/types.ts` + `renderer.tsx`) renders **web only**, not sent to Slack. (B) Slack BlockKit only for FIXED interaction vocab (ask_user/link-button/tool-approval) via `chat` SDK in `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/interaction-bridge.ts:352`. **No generic `json_template -> BlockKit`.** FUTURE separate goal: `json_template -> web chat / BlockKit` (explicitly OUT of this project).
103	- Conversation runtime persistence: each run = worker `child_process`; continuity via transcript-snapshot hydration at run START (`transcript-snapshot.ts`), not a live process; no mid-run injection hook in pi-ai. So "new events into context" = next-run / on-demand granularity, which is fine.
104	
105	## Multi-replica check (must hold for N>1)
106	All proposed reads/writes ride Postgres (`channel_messages`, `agent_channel_bindings`, `events`, `feeds`) — no new in-memory cross-pod state. The runtime in-between block (Stage B) is a per-run PG read, fine under N replicas. Cross-org preview routing stays the existing exception.
107	
108	## STAGED PLAN
109	**Stage 6 / "this project" = bindings-as-feed projection (ship first, small, no migration):**
110	1. Backend: a per-connection conversation-feed projection = `SELECT channel_id, max(occurred_at) lastActivityAt, count(*) FROM channel_messages WHERE connection_id=? GROUP BY channel_id`, decorated with `target` agent from `agent_channel_bindings` (match org+platform+channel_id+team_id). Expose as a "connection children" read (union: data feeds + conversation feeds) for the connection page.
111	2. Define the `Feed` interface + the two impls; data feeds = existing rows, conversation feeds = the virtual projection. Implement `recentActivity(since)` for the conversation impl over `channel_messages` (index-backed).
112	3. UI: generalize the feeds rail to render `kind:'conversation'` cards (label = channel name, status, lastActivity, target agent) alongside data feeds. Reuse `connection-feeds-rail.tsx` presentation.
113	4. Channel label resolution (G4): `conversations.info` lookup + cache (today shows raw `C0123…`).
114	
115	**Stage A = zero-touch install bootstrap (the "never see the app" flow):**
116	- Slack OAuth install -> create org if new + add connection (extend existing slack OAuth install path; `slack_installations` exists). Then enqueue backfill.
117	- **Backfill (NEW capability):** on install, `conversations.list` (channels/DMs the bot can see) + `conversations.history` per channel -> `channel_messages` (idempotent via the UNIQUE constraint). BOUNDED: recent-window and/or per-channel, throttled — do NOT firehose. Respect ACL/membership (only channels the bot is in).
118	- Each channel/DM then materializes as a conversation feed automatically (lazy projection — no feed rows to create).
119	
120	**Stage B = runtime "what happened in between" context block (retires the COMMON case of get_channel_history, NOT the tool):**
121	- New per-run, UNCACHED context block (can't ride the 5min static cache at `session-context.ts:220`) assembled gateway-side: query `channel_messages` for the channel delta since the agent's last run; inject into system context. This IS `recentActivity(since)` reused.
122	- **KEEP `get_channel_history`** (user explicitly unsure about deleting — do NOT delete). Auto-delta COMPLEMENTS it (passive catch-up for the routine case); tool stays for explicit/deep/cross-channel lookups. Reassess deletion later.
123	
124	## OPEN DECISIONS (confirm with user before building)
125	1. **Storage split semantics (#1, highest impact — drives embed load).** User said "new events stored in events but the conversation stored in our relevant table." Recommended reading: raw messages -> `channel_messages` (incl. backfill); only PROMOTED/distilled -> `events` (selective, existing seam). Confirm they don't mean "mirror every message into events" (that re-triggers embed congestion). Also clarify whether any NON-message Slack events (reactions, joins, file shares) should go to `events`.
126	2. **recordChannelMessages coupling (G2).** Does materializing a conversation feed IMPLY recording is on for that channel? (Recommend yes — else the feed is an empty shell.) Decides whether this project touches the capture/settings path or stays pure read-projection.
127	3. **Backfill scope.** Recent-window vs full-history; which channel types (public only? include private/DM?). Recommend bounded recent-window + bot-member channels only.
128	4. **Channel discovery (G1).** v1 = lazy materialization (feed appears after first captured message). Picker via `conversations.list` deferred — bundle with backfill since same API.
129	
130	## Cleanup / hygiene reminders for next agent
131	- Work in a worktree (`make task-setup NAME=conversation-feeds`), NOT main. Owletto UI changes -> read `packages/owletto/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` first.
132	- After agent-worker edits: `make clean-workers`. Validate: `make review`. Migrations (none expected for Stage 6) -> squawk gate.
133	- Cross-org preview route (org != connection org) stays the documented exception; don't force it under a connection.
134

Thought about this properly, and dug until I found the thing that reframes the whole question.

## The finding that changes the design

`chat_state_cache` isn't storing chat state. It's storing **Lobu's agent sessions — all of them**.

`SessionManager` → `StateAdapterSessionStore` → `ConversationStateStore` → the Chat SDK's `StateAdapter` → `chat_state_cache`. Its callers are `gateway/api/platform.ts` (the public agent API), `scheduled/jobs.ts`, `connectors/repair-agent.ts`. The prod rows confirm it: `session:personal-agent_watcher_5_run_793034`, `conversation_index:api_watcher_5:...` — watcher runs and API runs, nothing to do with chat.

Meanwhile the real `conversations` table exists, is well-shaped (PK `(org, agent_id, platform, conversation_id)`, `kind owned|platform`, `thread_id`, `last_activity_at`, sandbox pinning) and holds **68 rows**. The shadow KV holds **7,155 session + 7,155 conversation_index**, on a 24-hour TTL.

So a scheduled job's session lives in a third-party chat library's key-value store and expires. That's the inversion to fix, and it's also why "could we drop the Chat SDK" was the wrong question — today, dropping it would break cron.

## How I'd design it from scratch

**1. The system of record is a table; caches are disposable.**

`conversations` is the session and thread identity. Sessions become rows keyed by conversation, with an explicit lifecycle instead of a TTL. `StateAdapterSessionStore` dies. Nothing outside the chat path touches a chat library.

The lovely part: the KV is TTL'd at 24h, so **there is nothing to migrate**. Dual-write for a day, flip reads, drop the keys. That's the cheapest high-value change in the whole list.

**2. Persist-then-process on the inbound edge.**

Today the webhook does: hydrate instance (DB read + `setWebhook` + `registerCommands` network calls) → SDK verify/parse/dedupe/dispatch → bridge → routing → `INSERT INTO runs`. The 200 goes back independent of whether any of that committed. Every failure between the ACK and the INSERT is invisible. That's #2305, and it's this morning's "hey" — a 1,134ms request that returned 200 and left nothing behind.

From scratch:

```
POST /webhooks/:id
  → verify signature        (stateless, needs only the secret)
  → INSERT inbound row      (durable, dedup by UNIQUE constraint)
  → 200                     (~20ms, zero network calls)
                ↓ pg_notify
  → worker: parse → route → enqueue run
```

Three things fall out. Dedupe stops being a 5-minute cache key and becomes a UNIQUE constraint — and we **already have exactly that constraint**: `channel_messages_org_dedup (organization_id, connection_id, channel_id, platform_message_id)`. A dropped message becomes a row in a terminal state with a reason, never silence. And replay is re-running a row.

**3. Split "adapter" from "runner" — they're conflated today.**

An adapter is a pure function of config: wire codec plus card renderer. Cheap, stateless, cacheable per pod. A *runner* is a live process, and only two transports need one (Telegram polling, Slack Socket Mode). Today every connection gets a full `ManagedInstance` with a claim, a lease, a health sweep and an exclusive-runner tick — and `requireRunningInstance` gates even *outbound posting*, so replying to a message requires a hydrated instance with handlers registered and a webhook registered upstream.

Outbound should be `f(credentials, channel, thread, payload) → post`. The `requiresExclusiveStart` descriptor hook already exists and is already correct; the change is that webhook-mode connections stop getting an instance at all.

**4. One id namespace.** `channel_messages.connection_id` is `text` (a slug) while `connections.id` is `bigint`, which forces a slug-join documented in the chat-feeds plan. 80 rows in prod. You offered to migrate — this is the one to take.

**5. The transcript can't be optional.** `captureChannelMessage` is gated on `connection.settings.recordChannelMessages === true`, default off. If durable persistence is the delivery mechanism (point 2), capture can't be a setting. Retention becomes a deletion policy, which is what compliance actually wants anyway.

**6. Keep the SDK, scoped to two jobs:** platform wire protocol, and `Card` → Block Kit / inline keyboards. Pull everything domain-shaped out of it — sessions, routing, transcripts, dedupe, history. Then "should we drop the SDK" becomes a decision you can make later on its own merits, because nothing load-bearing depends on it anymore. That's the real goal: not removing it, making it *removable*.

## What I would deliberately not touch

The runs queue. One Postgres table, `SKIP LOCKED`, per-queue NOTIFY channels, heartbeat, stale sweep. That's the right design and rewriting it buys nothing.

The `conversations` table shape — it's already what the KV should have been.

The per-platform descriptor registry: 16-22 lines for whatsapp/gchat/teams/discord. That's a good abstraction earning its keep.

And I would **not** merge the `Card` DSL with `json_template`. They're different surfaces with genuinely different capability ceilings (5 chat elements vs 44 web node types) — collapsing them makes the chat vocabulary the ceiling for web. What's worth sharing is the *interaction contract* (button → action id → handler), not the layout vocabulary.

## Sequence

Each is independently shippable, in dependency order:

1. **Sessions out of the SDK KV** into `conversations`. No backfill (TTL), removes the chat dependency from cron and the agent API. Start here.
2. **Persist-then-process inbound.** The correctness win — it closes the class of bug that's now cost two sessions.
3. **`connection_id` text → bigint.** 80 rows.
4. **Collapse the three history stores** into `channel_messages`; delete the 48 dead `msg-history:` rows.
5. **Adapter/runner split.** Largest, and only worth it after 1-3 have shrunk what an "instance" has to be.

One honest caveat on step 2: the SDK wants to own `handleWebhook → dispatchToHandlers` as one call. Persist-then-process means verifying the signature ourselves, then feeding stored bytes to the SDK from a worker. The per-platform schemes are already documented in `chat-instance-manager.ts:1399-1410`, so this is known work, but it's the one piece I'd spike before committing to the sequencing — either we reconstruct a `Request` from stored bytes (works, but it's a fifth reach-in) or we own signature verification outright (cleaner, more code).

Confidence: **85** on the diagnosis — the session-in-chat-KV finding is traced from `core-services.ts` through `session-manager.ts` to live prod rows, and every table shape and row count here is read from the prod DB, not remembered. **65** on the sequencing, since step 2's SDK seam is unspiked and step 5's cost depends on what steps 1-3 leave behind.

Next actions:
1. Say go and I'll spike step 2's signature-verification seam — that's the one unknown gating the whole plan, and it's a day's work to resolve.
2. Or start with step 1, which has no unknowns, no backfill, and independently gets a chat library out of your cron path.
3. Either way worth writing this up as `docs/plans/chat-substrate.md` so it survives the session — the prior chat-feeds program has good material that this supersedes in places and depends on in others.
4. And regardless of all of it: the info-level "update ignored, type=X" log. Ten minutes, and it would have answered this morning's question in one line.

# Chat substrate refactor — plan (DRAFT, unreviewed)

Date: 2026-07-29. Author: Claude, from a live prod investigation of a silently-dropped
Telegram message. Status: proposal, nothing built.

## 0. Why this exists

Two production incidents in one week, same shape: an inbound chat message is accepted
(HTTP 200) and then vanishes with no log line and no row anywhere.

- **#2305 (fixed).** Chat SDK wrote its message-history cache inside `handleIncomingMessage`
  *before* `dispatchToHandlers`, unguarded; `processMessage` swallowed the throw and the
  webhook still answered 200. Only telegram+whatsapp set `persistMessageHistory`, which is
  exactly why Telegram DMs vanished while Slack worked on the same build.
- **2026-07-29 12:31 (unexplained).** `POST /lobu/api/v1/webhooks/85045b7a87884eea`, valid
  secret, 271 bytes, **200**, 1134ms — then no `Processing inbound message` and, decisively,
  **no `dedupe:telegram:6570514069:<id>` row** in `chat_state_cache`. Dedupe is written
  *inside* the SDK inbound path, so the update never entered it. Not reproducible: three
  synthetic replays and one real browser send all processed in 4-5s.

The common cause is not a specific bug. It is that **the inbound edge ACKs before anything
durable exists**, so a failure anywhere in a long in-request chain is indistinguishable from
success.

## 1. Ground truth (all read from prod `owletto` on 2026-07-29, not remembered)

### 1.1 The Chat SDK's KV store holds Lobu's agent sessions

`SessionManager` → `StateAdapterSessionStore` (`gateway/services/session-manager.ts:19`)
→ `ConversationStateStore` (`gateway/connections/conversation-state-store.ts:83`)
→ Chat SDK `StateAdapter` → `chat_state_cache`.

Callers of `SessionManager` include `gateway/api/platform.ts:260` (public agent API),
`scheduled/jobs.ts:469`, `connectors/repair-agent.ts:191`. None are chat.

Live key inventory, all `key_prefix = 'chat-conn'`:

| store | kind | rows | owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| cache | `conversation_index:` | 7155 | **Lobu** |
| cache | `session:` | 7155 | **Lobu** |
| cache | `dedupe:` | 297 | SDK |
| cache | `thread-backfilled:` | 31 | SDK |
| cache | `slack:` | 12 | SDK |
| cache | `history_index:` | 8 | Lobu |
| lists | `slack:` | 239 | SDK |
| lists | `history:` | 143 | Lobu |
| lists | `msg-history:` | 48 | SDK — **dead since #2305** |
| locks | — | 0 | SDK |
| subs | — | 68 | SDK |

Sample keys prove the scope: `session:personal-agent_watcher_5_run_793034`,
`conversation_index:api_watcher_5:personal-agent_watcher_5_run_793034` — watcher and API
runs, nothing to do with chat. TTL is 24h (`SESSION_TTL_MS`).

Meanwhile the real `conversations` table exists and holds **68 rows**:
PK `(organization_id, agent_id, platform, conversation_id)`, `kind CHECK IN ('owned','platform')`,
`thread_id`, `last_activity_at`, `archived_at`, sandbox pinning columns.

**So: a scheduled job's session lives in a third-party chat library's TTL'd KV. Removing the
Chat SDK today would break cron.**

### 1.2 The durable transcript is opt-in and off by default

`captureChannelMessage` (`gateway/connections/channel-transcript.ts`) is gated on
`connection.settings?.recordChannelMessages === true`
(`gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:913`). Default is off.

`channel_messages` already carries the correct dedupe key as a constraint:
`channel_messages_org_dedup UNIQUE (organization_id, connection_id, channel_id, platform_message_id)`.

### 1.3 Two id namespaces for one connection

`connections.id` is `bigint`. `channel_messages.connection_id` is `text` holding a slug
(`85045b7a87884eea`, or `agentconn-…`/`slackinst-…`). Prod volume: 80 rows total
(slack 68, telegram 12). The chat-feeds program documented a slug-join to bridge this.

### 1.4 Adapter and runner are conflated

Every connection gets a `ManagedInstance` with a claim (`connection_claims`), a lease, a
health sweep and an exclusive-runner tick. `requireRunningInstance`
(`chat-instance-manager.ts:1069`) gates **outbound posting** too, so replying needs a fully
hydrated instance with handlers registered and a webhook registered upstream.

`requiresExclusiveStart` (per-platform descriptor hook) already correctly identifies the
transports that need a live process (Telegram polling, Slack Socket Mode). Webhook-mode
connections do not, but get the whole apparatus anyway.

Observed cost: the 12:31 webhook request performed instance hydration *inline*, including
`setWebhook` and `registerCommands` network calls to Telegram — 1134ms inside the ACK path.

### 1.5 SDK surface is small; the glue is not

Ten files import from `chat`. The whole surface is: the `Chat` class (2 files), the card DSL
`Card/CardText/Actions/Button/LinkButton` (4 files, **67 call sites** spanning notifications,
guardrails, approvals, activity feed, `manage_behaviors`), the `StateAdapter` *type* (we
implement it, 400 lines), and `CardElement`.

Per-platform module cost: whatsapp 16, gchat 17, teams 22, discord 22, slack 100,
telegram 401 lines. Around it: `gateway/connections` 13,029 lines, `gateway/orchestration`
5,145 lines.

Of `chat-instance-manager.ts`'s ~50 methods, about six touch the SDK. The rest is connection
lifecycle and survives SDK removal unchanged.

Prod platform usage: slack 8 connections (3 active, 5 paused), telegram 1. Discord, Teams,
GChat, WhatsApp: zero connections ever. `channel_messages`: slack 68, telegram 12.

We already bypass the SDK where it does not fit: `slack-web.ts` (283 lines, dependency-free
`fetch`, header says explicitly "NOT `@slack/web-api`, NOT the chat adapter") for onboarding
DMs and the authz channel-membership sync.

### 1.6 Existing SDK reach-ins (4)

1. `disableSdkMessageHistory` — `Object.defineProperty` over a readonly SDK flag
   (`platforms/shared.ts:26`). This is #2305's fix.
2. Synthesized private `_currentMessage` (`chat-response-bridge.ts:61`). Comment: "Passing
   `{}` crashes the SDK; passing `undefined` silently disables the recipient hint."
3. `(chat as any).createThread` called with four positional args including a bare boolean
   (`platforms/shared.ts:63`) — not on the public type.
4. `resolveChatTarget`'s four-step fallback, whose last step exists "so the response still
   lands somewhere instead of silently disappearing".

## 2. Target design

### P1 — The system of record is a table; caches are disposable

`conversations` owns session and thread identity. Sessions become rows with an explicit
lifecycle, not KV keys with a TTL. `StateAdapterSessionStore` is deleted. Nothing outside
the chat path depends on a chat library.

### P2 — Persist-then-process on the inbound edge

```
POST /webhooks/:id
  → verify signature          stateless, needs only the secret
  → INSERT inbound row        durable; dedupe by UNIQUE constraint
  → 200                       no network calls, no hydration
              ↓ pg_notify
  → worker: parse → route → enqueue run
```

Consequences: dedupe stops being a 5-minute cache key and becomes the constraint we already
have; a dropped message becomes a row in a terminal state with a reason instead of silence;
replay is re-running a row; the ACK path stops making network calls.

### P3 — Split adapter from runner

- **Adapter** = pure function of config → wire codec + card renderer. Stateless, per-pod
  cacheable, no claim, no lease, no health sweep.
- **Runner** = a live process, only for transports where `requiresExclusiveStart` is true.
- **Outbound** = `f(credentials, channel, thread, payload) → post`. No `requireRunningInstance`.

### P4 — One id namespace

`channel_messages.connection_id` becomes `bigint` FK → `connections.id`. 80 rows.

### P5 — Transcript capture is mandatory

If durable persistence is the delivery mechanism (P2), it cannot be a per-connection setting.
`recordChannelMessages` is removed; retention becomes a deletion policy, which is what
compliance actually wants.

### P6 — Scope the SDK to what only it does

Platform wire protocol and `Card` → Block Kit / inline keyboards. Everything domain-shaped
(sessions, routing, transcripts, dedupe, history) comes out. The goal is not to remove the
SDK — it is to make it *removable*, so that decision can later be made on its own merits.

## 3. Explicit non-goals

- **Do not rewrite the runs queue.** One Postgres table, `SKIP LOCKED`, per-queue NOTIFY
  channels, heartbeat, stale sweep. Correct as-is.
- **Do not delete discord/teams/gchat/whatsapp.** Low prod usage is not delete evidence;
  they are advertised product surface, and cost 16-22 lines each *because* the SDK carries
  them.
- **Do not merge the `Card` DSL with `json_template`.** 5 chat elements vs 44 web node types;
  collapsing makes the chat vocabulary the ceiling for web. Share the *interaction contract*
  (action id → handler), not the layout vocabulary.
- **Do not change the `conversations` table shape.** It is already what the KV should have been.
- **Do not touch the per-platform descriptor registry.** Good abstraction, earning its keep.

## 4. Sequence

Each step independently shippable, in dependency order.

**Step 1 — Sessions out of the SDK KV into `conversations`.**
No backfill required: the KV is TTL'd at 24h, so dual-write for a day, flip reads, drop the
keys. Deletes `StateAdapterSessionStore`, removes the chat-library dependency from cron and
the public agent API. Highest value, zero unknowns.

**Step 2 — Persist-then-process inbound.** The correctness win; closes the incident class.
See open question Q1.

**Step 3 — `channel_messages.connection_id` text → bigint FK.** 80 rows.

**Step 4 — Collapse the three history stores** (`channel_messages`, `chat_state_lists`
`history:`, dead `msg-history:`) onto `channel_messages`. Delete the 48 orphan rows.
~12 call sites.

**Step 5 — Adapter/runner split.** Largest; only worth doing after 1-3 shrink what an
"instance" must be.

**Step 0 (independent, ~10 min, do regardless)** — `handleWebhook` logs
`Inbound platform webhook` but never what it did with the update. Add an info-level
"update ignored, type=X". Every SDK skip path logs at `debug` and prod runs at `info`, so
these drops are currently invisible. This would have answered the 12:31 question in one line.

## 5. Open questions / risks

- **Q1 (gates step 2).** The SDK wants to own `handleWebhook → dispatchToHandlers` as one
  call. Persist-then-process means verifying signatures ourselves, then feeding stored bytes
  to the SDK from a worker. Either reconstruct a `Request` from stored bytes+headers (works,
  but is a fifth reach-in) or own signature verification outright (cleaner, more code). The
  per-platform schemes are documented at `chat-instance-manager.ts:1399-1410`. **Needs a
  spike before sequencing is final.**
- **Q2.** Does anything depend on session TTL expiry as a *feature* (implicit session reset
  after 24h idle)? If so, P1 must model it explicitly rather than inherit it.
- **Q3.** Step 5 changes multi-replica behaviour for outbound. Today `requireRunningInstance`
  incidentally guarantees a hydrated, row-versioned view of the connection. A stateless
  outbound path must re-establish that guarantee (config version check on send).
- **Q4.** Step 3 touches `resolveBoundChannelRows` / `ChannelBindingService`, which the
  chat-feeds program already modified. Check for conflicts with in-flight work there.
